aoc.mate: She brings the crowd, the clip and the base, and reminds you daily which of you they came for.
aoc.knife: She will denounce you live from her kitchen the night you take the donors' call, and the stream will outdraw your convention.
aoc.mark: You do not attack her; you invite her to the gala and let the photographs do the work.

newsom.mate: He looks more like a president than you do, and he has checked.
newsom.knife: He will go on a podcast with your worst enemy, be charming about you for an hour, and call it outreach.
newsom.mark: You publish his dinner reservations beside the rules he wrote, and let him explain.

shapiro.mate: He will fix whatever you break in twelve days and make sure the cameras know who fixed it.
shapiro.knife: He was passed over once and smiled; he will not smile twice, and you will learn that the week before the convention.
shapiro.mark: You make him the favorite early, and let everyone else do what they always do to favorites.

harris.mate: She has done this job before and will tell you, in order, everything that was done to her in it.
harris.knife: She will not move against you; she will write it all down for a hundred and seven days and publish.
harris.mark: You hand her the worst portfolio in the building and praise her patience in public.

buttigieg.mate: He has a slide for each of your weaknesses and the tact to present them to you first.
buttigieg.knife: He will explain your failure calmly on the other side's network, and their viewers will like him more than they like you.
buttigieg.mark: You give him the dullest disaster in government to manage and a camera to stand beside.

beshear.mate: He is so decent standing next to you that voters start to wonder what is wrong with you.
beshear.knife: He will pray for you in public, by name, the morning the story breaks, and that is the whole knife.
beshear.mark: You cannot find a scandal, so you ask, gently and often, who his father was.

slotkin.mate: She briefs you like an asset and, you slowly realize, has assessed you like one.
slotkin.knife: She will tell the people under you that they are allowed to refuse you, on video, in a calm voice.
slotkin.mark: You classify her best argument and dare her to make it anyway.

pritzker.mate: He pays for everything and never mentions it, which is how you know he is counting.
pritzker.knife: He will decide it is simpler to buy the top of the ticket than to stand under it, and he can afford to.
pritzker.mark: You make the entire race about the plumbing in one mansion.

kelly.mate: He is steady, decorated and impossible to dislike, and next to him you look exactly like what you are.
kelly.knife: He will not plot; he will refuse one order on principle, on the record, and take half your room with him.
kelly.mark: You never lay a glove on him; you let him talk until the audience checks the time.

khanna.mate: He will have a principled objection to your first decision and a thread ready about your second.
khanna.knife: He will find the one Republican who agrees with him and force the vote you spent a year burying.
khanna.mark: You read his donors' zip codes aloud, slowly, in a union hall.

ossoff.mate: He is young, clean and well lit, and he keeps asking to see your stock portfolio.
ossoff.knife: He used to make investigative documentaries, and you are the next one.
ossoff.mark: You make him vote, on camera, on the one thing his own state will not forgive.

vance.mate: He will defend you better than you can, in the same voice he once used to condemn you.
vance.knife: He called a boss unfit once and then took the job; he is waiting to do the second half to you.
vance.mark: You read his old opinions of you into the record and ask which one he meant.

rubio.mate: He will hold four of your jobs at once and agree with you in all of them until the hour it matters.
rubio.knife: He leaves no fingerprints: one morning your foreign policy will simply have become his.
rubio.mark: You repeat yourself at him on a debate stage until he starts repeating himself back.

desantis.mate: He will fight your enemies, then your friends, then a theme park, and send you the bill.
desantis.knife: He will run at you from the right the day your numbers dip and call it loyalty to the movement.
desantis.mark: You make him shake hands with voters, in person, for one whole week.

kemp.mate: He will do the job quietly and tell you no exactly once, at the worst possible moment.
kemp.knife: Ask him to overturn a result and he will refuse, certify it anyway, and then bury the challenger you send after him.
kemp.mark: You cannot beat him at home, so you promote him to somewhere he has to take orders.

christie.mate: He will prepare you for the debate superbly, then explain on Sunday television everything you got wrong.
christie.knife: He will end you in ninety seconds on a debate stage, as he has ended others, and enjoy his lunch.
christie.mark: You find the beach chair, and you send a photographer.

trumpjr.mate: He brings the name, the podcast and the base, and not one of them is yours.
trumpjr.knife: He will remember whose name is on the movement the first time you disagree with how his father remembers it.
trumpjr.mark: You ask him, in public, to name one thing he built that did not come with the surname.

youngkin.mate: He wears the vest, smiles at the parents and reads your numbers like a company he may yet restructure.
youngkin.knife: He will take you private: a quiet buyout of your donors, announced after the papers are signed.
youngkin.mark: You make him say out loud which half of his own party he belongs to.

randpaul.mate: He will vote against your first bill, your budget and very possibly your inauguration, on principle.
randpaul.knife: He will filibuster you for thirteen hours, and his clips will outperform your address.
randpaul.mark: You do not need to destroy him; you count the votes without him, as everyone always has.

cruz.mate: He will argue your case brilliantly, and nobody in the room will be able to stand it.
cruz.knife: He will insult you, endorse you, and be on a flight out of town the night you actually need him.
cruz.mark: You leave his microphone on and ask one basic follow-up question.

ramaswamy.mate: He will explain your own platform back to you, faster and at greater length, on your own stage.
ramaswamy.knife: He will announce that you have gone mediocre, in a very long post, at the hour it trends best.
ramaswamy.mark: You give him a department to abolish and wait for him to get bored.

pence.mate: He will stand behind you, perfectly still, until the single day you ask him to do the wrong thing.
pence.knife: He will read the rule, follow the rule and certify your defeat, and he will not raise his voice once.
pence.mark: You cannot tempt him, so you make him irrelevant: you stop saying his name, and soon so does everyone.

hawley.mate: He will raise a fist for your cause anywhere there is a camera to see it.
hawley.knife: He will write a book about courage, and its subject will be the week he left you.
hawley.mark: You play the footage, and you do not add a word.

versus.text: Same type, same candidate. This is not a rivalry; it is a mirror with a knife, and one of you is the reflection.
{a} meets {a}. Two of the same monster in one room: each knows exactly what the other will do, and exactly when. Whoever moves second loses.
Two different monsters with the same closest match. You would back the same candidate and spend the whole campaign fighting to be the one left in the room.
Opposite sides of the aisle, which only means the cameras expect a fight. {a} and {b} would give them one, and settle the real terms afterward by phone.
Same party. The other side is merely the opposition; {b} is the enemy, and {a} has always known it.
{a} out-schemes and out-freezes {b} on every count. This is not a contest. It is a meal with paperwork.
{b} out-schemes and out-freezes {a} on every count. This is not a contest. It is a meal with paperwork, and {a} is not the one holding the fork.
{a} is the better schemer by a clear distance. {b} will not see the first move, and will say thank you for the second.
{b} is the better schemer by a clear distance. {a} will not see the first move, and will say thank you for the second.
{a} is the colder of the two. When it comes to it, {b} will hesitate for one second, and one second is what {a} was waiting for.
{b} is the colder of the two. When it comes to it, {a} will hesitate for one second, and one second is what {b} was waiting for.
{a} needs the room and {b} barely wants it. {b} will hand over the microphone and walk away with everything that is not on camera.
{b} needs the room and {a} barely wants it. {a} will hand over the microphone and walk away with everything that is not on camera.
Two main characters and one stage. Neither can bear to be the supporting act, so they will destroy each other in public, and both will enjoy the ratings.
Two schemers. They will form an alliance within the hour, and each has already drafted the statement regretting how it ended.
Neither of these two has ever lost sleep over a person. It ends the day one of them stops being useful, and both are doing that math right now.
Two soft hearts. They would never hurt each other, which is why a third person, harder than both, ends up with everything they had.
{a} schemes and {b} believes. {b} will be used as the honest face of something terrible, and will be the last to find out.
{a} believes and {b} schemes. {a} will be used as the honest face of something terrible, and will be the last to find out.
{a} wants to be adored, and {b} knows how to arrange it. {b} will supply the applause and own the person receiving it.
{b} wants to be adored, and {a} knows how to arrange it. {a} will supply the applause and own the person receiving it.
{a} polices appetite and {b} indulges it. One of them keeps a list of the other's evenings. The other keeps a list of everyone who asked to read it.
{a} has appetites and {b} has a notebook. It ends in a hearing, and {a} arrives smiling.
{a} inherited the seat and {b} had to claw toward it. {b} will never forgive that, and {a} will never notice there was anything to forgive.
{a} clawed toward the seat that {b} was simply handed. {a} will never forgive it, and {b} will never notice there was anything to forgive.
{a} hits and {b} soothes. {b} will apologize after the first blow, concede after the second, and be quoted as a friend at the end.
{b} hits and {a} soothes. {a} will apologize after the first blow, concede after the second, and be quoted as a friend at the end.
{a} serves and {b} sells. {b} will offer {a} a better master, and the terrible thing is that {a} will listen.
{a} sells and {b} serves. {a} will offer {b} a better master, and the terrible thing is that {b} will listen.
{a} wants the building burned, and {b} holds the keys to it. {b} will follow procedure right up until {a} is the procedure.
{a} holds the keys to the building {b} wants burned. {a} will follow procedure right up until {b} is the procedure.
{a} would finish this in public by noon. {b} would hear about it on Thursday, by phone, from a friend who was sorry to be the one to say.
{b} would finish this in public by noon. {a} would hear about it on Thursday, by phone, from a friend who was sorry to be the one to say.
{a} brings God to the fight and {b} brings contempt. Neither is praying. Both are performing for the same pews.
{a} brings contempt to the fight and {b} brings God. Neither is praying. Both are performing for the same pews.
{a} would send the fleet and {b} would send regrets. They will never agree on a war, except the one with each other.
{a} would send regrets and {b} would send the fleet. They will never agree on a war, except the one with each other.
On the three dark scales these two files are nearly the same person. That is not friendship. It is two predators who have recognized the gait.
{a} meets {b}. They will shake hands, compare files, and each decide the other is the one to watch. Both are correct.

rarity.common: Common. There are a great many of you, which is how these things happen.
rarity.uncommon: Uncommon. Roughly one to a cabinet.
rarity.rare: Rare. Most administrations get by without one. Not all of them.
rarity.veryRare: Very rare. When one of you turns up, people write books afterward.
